items.title: Hong Kong reviews river fees as mainland ports lure cargo away
items.original_title: Hong Kong reviews river fees as mainland ports lure cargo away
items.summary: Hong Kong is reviewing permit fees charged to river trade vessels as it seeks to maintain its port’s competitiveness amid growing competition from mainland Chinese terminals in Guangzhou and Shenzhen. The secretary for transport and logistics, Chan Mei-po, announced the review in a written reply to the Legislative Council on Wednesday. China-flagged vessels carry containers between ports in the Pearl River Delta and Hong Kong, where cargo may be transferred to ocean-going vessels for onward shipment. Hong Kong operates a multiple-entry permit scheme, allowing operators to make up to 10 port entries within a month for a fee equivalent to five single-entries – the “buy five, get five free” system. Ms Chan said: “The Action Plan on Maritime and Port Development Strategy proposes various measures to strengthen Hong Kong’s position as a regional transhipment hub, including reviewing the permit fees charged to river trade vessels in order to maintain the competitiveness and attractiveness of the port to the industry. We have completed a preliminary review and are now discussing the matter with relevant departments, with the details to be released in due course.” Laden container movements between Hong Kong and mainland China account for more than 40% of the territory’s annual laden container throughput.

According to the International Transport Workers’ Federation, many crews face severe shortages of food, drinking water, fuel, medical assistance, and unpaid wages, while more than 40 sailors have reportedly been killed. items.title: Poland has EU’s second-highest electricity prices accounting for cost of living
items.original_title: Poland has EU’s second-highest electricity prices accounting for cost of living
items.summary: Poland had the second-highest household electricity prices in the European Union in the first half of 2026 after adjusting for differences in the cost of living, new Eurostat data show. In nominal terms, Polish households paid €29.99 per 100 kilowatt-hours (kWh) for electricity in the first half of 2026. However, when adjusted for purchasing power standards (PPS), which account for differences in the cost of living, Poland ranked second in the EU, at 41.12 PPS per 100 kWh. One reason why electricity prices in Poland remain high is the country’s continued reliance on coal, which last year generated just over half of power , by far the highest proportion in the EU. These costs contribute to the high taxes and levies included in household electricity bills, which accounted for 39% of the final price in Poland in the first half of 2026. Without taxes and levies, the nominal price of electricity in Poland would have been just under €16 per 100 kWh, below the EU average of €20.27.

items.original_title: Upswing in domestic demand gives railfreight operators a revenue boost
items.summary: Union Pacific led the way on the North American containerised rail freight front over the three months to October, amid all the noise surrounding its pending acquisition of Norfolk Southern – but it was not alone in enjoying a bountiful summer. In general, North American intermodal operators benefited from an upswing in domestic freight demand and a continuing tightening in the trucking market, with revenues up for all four of the major carriers. Boasting a 27% year-on-year revenue increase, Union Pacific took home some $1.52bn over the quarter, with volumes up 11%, to 956,000 carloads, and pointing specifically to reduced trucking capacity as behind the gains. “We’re very optimistic about the opportunities as we close this year and go into next on the domestic intermodal side,” she told investors, adding that the tightening in trucking could prove a boost when yields come up for renewal. Not one to miss out, Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) also reported double-digit revenue growth in intermodal, up 22% year on year to $583m, as volumes rose 9%, to 489,800 carloads. Together with the increased traffic, stronger pricing likely played its part in driving the improvement for the Canadian operator that saw its revenue per carload increase 12% year on year, to $1,190.

items.title: Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration
items.original_title: Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration
items.summary: Norway has detained a Chinese-owned heavy-lift vessel sanctioned for its role in delivering equipment to Russia’s Arctic LNG 2 project, in what appears to be the first known detention in the Arctic of a Chinese vessel linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. The Ya Qing Hai Yang was detained after Norwegian inspectors found that it lacked valid flag-state registration and required certificates, the Norwegian Maritime Authority said. The case is a notable enforcement action against a vessel with documented ties to Russia’s sanctioned energy sector, although authorities say the detention was based on maritime safety and registration deficiencies rather than the ship’s sanctions status. “During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel did not have a valid flag registration and lacked the required certificates,” Dag Inge Aarhus, the authority’s communications director said last week. “The vessel has therefore been detained until further notice.” The vessel remains off the Vesterålen Islands as of November 3. The ship must establish valid registration with a flag state and obtain the necessary certificates before Norwegian authorities can complete the inspection and consider its release. The detention appears to be the first publicly documented case of Norway holding a vessel sailing under an invalid flag registration. The United States sanctioned the vessel’s operator and related entities in January 2025 .

Stark plans to develop the Vanta 24 in the UK and Germany, and hired Stephen Brian, a former nuclear submarine commander for the British Royal Navy, to run the company’s naval operations. He described Vanta 24 as a versatile vessel designed to escort warships or surveil on its own, replacing the labor-intensive work of monitoring coastlines and subsea cables. In June, it reached a valuation of €3.2 billion ($3.6 billion) and has grown to more than 700 employees. Luciana Lixandru, a partner with Sequoia Capital, said the Silicon Valley investor backed Stark because it believes the company will be one of Europe’s few defense newcomers to compete with prime contractors.

items.original_title: Fears a strike at San Pedro Bay ports could worsen congestion
items.summary: Concern is rising among cargo owners and logistics providers that a strike at the Los Angeles/Long Beach port complex could turbo-charge the congestion there. About 250 watchmen, who perform security-related duties at container terminals at the twin ports, are poised to walk off the job at 5pm Pacific time on Wednesday, should last-minute contract negotiations between the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) and the Pacific Maritime Association (PMA) fail to reach agreement. Watchmen have been working under contract extensions since the agreement expired in July 2025. Union members had authorised a strike for 1 November, but both sides agreed to extend negotiations until 4 November. According to the PMA, a work stoppage would affect 85% of the container traffic at the port of Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles. Ted Chen, ocean freight and trade compliance director at logistics provider Dimerco, said there was a high likelihood that other port employees would support the strike, a concern echoed by forwarder Woodland Group. The actual scale of any interruption would depend on the terminals affected, the participation of other workers and the duration of industrial action.” ,Moreover, the disruption would aggravate congestion that has resulted in extended dwell times for rail cargo at several of the affected terminals.

items.title: Offshore operators should not wait for EU ETS clarity to act on emissions data
items.original_title: Offshore operators should not wait for EU ETS clarity to act on emissions data
items.summary: EU MRV has applied to offshore vessels of 400 GT and above since 1 January 2025, and vessels of 5,000 GT and above are scheduled to enter the EU ETS from the 2027 reporting period. On 17 July 2026, the European Commission published proposals that would revise the MRV framework from 1 January 2029 and bring offshore vessels between 400 and 5,000 GT into the ETS from 2031. These are not final, however, and must still pass through the legislative process. The International Marine Contractors Association (IMCA) has welcomed the recognition of offshore-specific terminology and operational realities, but says more clarity is needed on ports of call, cross-border operations and how the EU and UK ETS interact. In August, Norway’s Ministry of Climate and Environment confirmed that FuelEU Maritime and ReFuelEU Aviation, previously expected to take effect later this year, will not enter into force for Norway before 1 January 2028. From 2029, companies operating on the Norwegian continental shelf must reduce the greenhouse gas intensity of ships used in oil and gas activity, starting at 10% for 2029-2031 and rising in stages to 40% for 2038-2040. Rystad Energy estimates close to 300 offshore vessels fall within scope, and that most of them, including LNG dual-fuel units, would miss the first threshold based on how they operate today.

items.original_title: When the ship pays back before the owner does
items.summary: Fuel-saving retrofits can pay for themselves long before the shipowner who funded them sees a return. A new BIMCO contract seeks to resolve shipping’s longstanding divide between who pays for efficiency and who pockets the savings. Alex Byelyavtsev reports. If the owner pays to burn less, the immediate fuel saving shows up first in the charterer’s accounts. If the charterer pays, the steel stays on someone else’s ship when the fixture ends. If the owner funds the whole amount and keeps half of that saving, the owner’s simple payback stretches to about 4.9 years. Yet the owner would have recovered only $1.44m, leaving $910,000 still unrecovered when the fixture ended. The ship can reach payback before the investor does. Under BIMCO’s ETS clause for time charter, the charterer provides and pays for the allowances corresponding to the vessel’s emissions during the charter period.

items.original_title: Alternative fuels comprised 12% of NYK’s marine fuel mix in 2025
items.summary: Low greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions marine fuels accounted for 12.2% of Japanese shipping company NYK Line’s total fuel consumption in the financial year 2025 (FY2025). Japanese shipping company Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK Line) continued to expand its dual-fuel fleet, operating 35 such vessels in the previous financial year, up from 26 in 2024. The figures exclude LNG carriers and LNG-ready vessels, the company said. Biofuels comprised the largest share of NYK Line’s marine fuel mix during the mentioned period, followed by LNG. Biofuel consumption rose to 297,000 mt in FY2025, continuing an upward trajectory from 251,000 mt a year earlier and a baseline of 6,000 mt in FY2023. The shipping company is actively “increasing the use of biofuels and alternative fuels available today to achieve immediate GHG emissions reductions.” NYK Line’s progressive shift toward low-emission marine fuels helped the company to reduce its emissions by 260,000 mt of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) in FY2025, it said. The shipping company laid a groundwork for broader biofuel adoption with the launch of a 12-month B100 (100% biofuel) pilot project aboard a car carrier in May 2026. “In addition to the B100 trial, NYK is advancing the evaluation and verification of Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) as part of efforts to expand the range of sustainable biofuel options,” it said.

items.original_title: Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
items.summary: A broad coalition of maritime, agricultural, manufacturing, retail and logistics organizations is urging the Trump administration to permanently suspend U.S. port fees targeting China-linked vessels, warning that reinstating the charges would raise costs for American businesses, hurt exporters and disrupt global supply chains. In an October 30 letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer , the coalition welcomed the proposed two-month extension of the Section 301 vessel fee suspension through January 9, 2027, but called on Washington to go further and eliminate the charges permanently. Because Chinese-built ships account for a significant share of global shipping capacity, the coalition warned that the impact would extend well beyond Chinese shipping companies, affecting vessel deployments and transportation costs for American importers and exporters. The coalition also challenged the idea that port fees would meaningfully rebuild America’s struggling commercial shipbuilding industry. The latest industry appeal follows the Trump administration’s October 23 proposal to extend the suspension through January 9, 2027, as Washington and Beijing continue negotiations over China’s dominance of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors. The push for a permanent suspension comes amid competing pressure from lawmakers and maritime labor unions, which argue that the fees are necessary to counter China’s state-supported shipbuilding industry and encourage investment in American shipyards.

The LEKHRAIB, the first of six 174,000-cubic-meter LNG carriers ordered by CMES from South Korea’s Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI), was named during ceremonies held on Geoje Island and in Busan. The vessel will provide long-term LNG transportation services for QatarEnergy. In addition to the six vessels built by Samsung Heavy Industries, CMES secured long-term transportation contracts for four larger 271,000-cubic-meter QC MAX carriers, which are being built by China’s Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding. LNG carriers are among the most technologically demanding commercial vessels, as they transport natural gas at temperatures of around minus 162 C. The LEKHRAIB features a GTT Mark III Flex membrane containment system, with a designed daily boil-off rate of no more than 0.085 percent, as well as dual-fuel engines. South Korean shipbuilders have long held a strong position in large LNG carrier construction, while Chinese shipyards have been expanding their capabilities and securing more orders for advanced vessels, Wang Peng, an associate researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times.

items.summary: Singapore-based Asia Break Bulk has secured four 12,600 dwt multipurpose heavylift newbuildings through a long-term deal with Schoeller Holdings. The COLI Group-controlled carrier said the Octopus-type vessels, designed by China’s CSSC-SDARI, will feature two 250-tonne cranes capable of tandem lifts of up to 500 tonnes. The first ship is scheduled for delivery in October 2028, with the remaining three to follow. The vessels will have a single box-shaped cargo hold measuring more than 89 m in length, while a forward-mounted superstructure will provide additional deck space for oversized cargo. Asia Break Bulk, which marks its 20th anniversary this year, has traditionally operated semi-liner services connecting Asia and Europe. Maximilian Fischer, general manager at Asia Break Bulk, said customers are increasingly looking for shorter transit times and direct access to ports with draft restrictions, reducing the need for costly and time-consuming transshipments. Schoeller Holdings is backing the newbuilding programme, while Columbia Shipmanagement will supervise construction and take over technical and crew management once the vessels enter service. The deal adds another chapter to Cyprus-based Schoeller’s extensive investment in multipurpose and heavylift tonnage. Earlier this year, the group booked two 32,000 dwt MPP vessels at China’s CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding for delivery in 2029, extending a relationship with the yard dating back to 2008.

items.summary: Commercial shipping in the western Indian Ocean has been warned of a potential new piracy threat after armed attackers seized an Iranian fishing vessel off Somalia and moved it towards a busy maritime traffic lane. The Azini was hijacked on Thursday, October 29, off the northeastern Somali coast, with 21 Iranian crewmembers and two Somali security guards aboard. According to a Puntland Maritime Police Force officer, 12 pirates boarded the vessel between Bandar Bayla and Hafun. The captain reportedly managed to send a distress voice message to another vessel before communications were lost. The Maritime Security Centre – Indian Ocean (MSCIO) subsequently tracked the vessel moving eastwards, with its latest reported position at 09°47’N, 055°45’E, approaching a commercial shipping route. Maritime security authorities are particularly concerned that the fishing vessel could be used as a mothership, allowing pirates to launch attacks against merchant ships hundreds of miles offshore. The seizure comes amid a worrying resurgence of piracy around Somalia. According to the Associated Press, six commercial vessels had been hijacked between April and August. In September, Puntland security forces recovered the tanker Honour 25 after a lengthy hijacking, with five crewmembers reportedly killed during the incident.

items.title: Russia moves to bar ageing foreign ships from its ports
items.original_title: Russia moves to bar ageing foreign ships from its ports
items.summary: Russia has formally put proposed restrictions on ageing merchant ships out for public consultation, seeking to bar foreign-flagged vessels older than 40 years from its ports as Moscow tightens oversight of the fleet carrying its seaborne trade. The transport ministry published the draft legislation, proposing a separate 50-year threshold for Russian-flagged ships, with transitional arrangements tied to the validity of their classification certificates. Foreign-flagged vessels older than 30 years would also face annual inspections to confirm compliance with safety and environmental requirements. The proposed rules would assess vessels against their inspection and repair records, technical condition and insurance coverage. Cargo transportation contracts would also have to specify the use of compliant ships, while marine terminal operators would assume additional responsibilities for ensuring vessels meet the requirements. The move advances an initiative Moscow has been developing for more than a year. The transport ministry outlined the proposed 40-year limit for foreign ships in July, alongside plans for tighter oversight of older Russian tonnage. However, the government faces a substantial fleet replacement challenge. Deputy transport minister Alexander Poshivay said last month that restrictions would not be adopted until the country was confident replacement vessels could be secured, acknowledging that domestic shipyards face constraints on capacity, pricing and construction times.

items.original_title: Maritime CEO Forum: Dry bulk owners eye generational rate rally
items.summary: Dry bulk shipping could be approaching a generational freight rate rally as surging West African mineral exports transform tonne-mile demand, according to shipowners speaking at last week’s Maritime CEO Forum in Monaco, although concerns remain over the rapid expansion of Chinese shipbuilding capacity. Around 5 mteu of new capacity has been ordered in each of the past three years, pushing the orderbook-to-fleet ratio to approximately 45%, its highest level since 2009. Ultimately, the 2027 outcome will depend on whether demand growth, slow steaming and congestion can absorb capacity faster than new ships enter service. Overcapacity is, in our view, unavoidable. More than 70% expect some degree of overcapacity in 2027, with 56.7% anticipating a moderate surplus and 14.2% predicting significant overcapacity. Blank sailings, service adjustments and other measures can help contain the surplus, but respondents appear unconvinced that carriers can fully offset the delivery pipeline. Cargo demand attracted just 11.7%, while demolitions accounted for only 1.3%, suggesting that neither stronger demand nor the removal of older tonnage is widely expected to be the decisive factor. items.original_title: Taiwan Says China Harassing Shipping With East Coast Patrol
items.summary: A Taiwan Coast Guard patrol vessel moves in Keelung, as China conducts "Justice Mission 2025" military drills around Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan, December 30, 2025. REUTERS/Ann Wang TAIPEI, Nov 1 (Reuters) – China’s Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan’s east coast and trying to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding it had sent its own ships to keep watch. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island’s east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Taiwan’s Coast Guard said China’s “attempts to harass ships at sea through radio communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality.” “Our country holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan, and China has absolutely no jurisdiction over any of Taiwan’s waters,” it added. China on Saturday also sent another Coast Guard ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands, which are strategically located at the top of the South China Sea, Taiwan’s Coast Guard said separately. Taiwan has so far this year “expelled” Chinese Coast Guard vessels from Pratas waters 13 times, it added.

items.original_title: StormGeo acquires Portchain to advance Just-in-Time voyage optimization at scale
items.summary: Portchain, headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, is now part of StormGeo, Alfa Laval’s digital arm for weather intelligence, voyage optimization and fleet performance. The deal was closed on 30 October 2026. Portchain connects container carriers and terminals through shared operational data. StormGeo’s Voyage Intelligence combines voyage optimization, vessel-performance insight and expert route guidance to help operators optimize for arrival time, fuel consumption or the balance between the two. This is the foundation for Just-in-Time voyage optimization at scale: turning a change in the terminal plan into a timely voyage decision. “By combining weather and voyage insights with up-to-date information from ports and terminals, we can help customers plan and act with greater confidence, improve efficiency from sea to port, and make meaningful progress towards their environmental goals.” “Our ambition is to help make maritime operations more predictable, efficient and sustainable,” says Niels Kristiansen, CEO of Portchain. “Joining StormGeo gives us the opportunity to bring voyage optimization and port call coordination closer together, helping customers get more value from the decisions they already make. Portchain will operate as an independent company under StormGeo for the next few years and will later be fully integrated into StormGeo’s portfolio. Existing Portchain customers will see no disruption to their service, and the combined offering will be available through StormGeo.

items.title: Saudi Arabia tanker oil loadings rise to highest level since February
items.original_title: Saudi Arabia tanker oil loadings rise to highest level since February
items.summary: Nine very large crude carriers collected oil cargoes at Saudi Arabia’s Persian Gulf export facilities on Wednesday, marking the highest level of activity at these terminals since hostilities began in the region at the end of February. Images from the European Union’s Sentinel 2 orbiter showed the nine VLCCs moored at Saudi berths. The vessels have a combined transportation capacity of approximately 18 million barrels. items.title: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?
items.original_title: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?
items.summary: In September we borrowed a Led Zeppelin title to describe China’s crude stockpile, a levee holding backthe import shortfall created by the closure of Hormuz. One month on, the wateris still falling, Gulf crude has rambled on around the Strait, and the questionis what it will cost to rebuild. China’s customs crudeimports were 9.03 mbpd in September, broadly flat on August, while refineryruns climbed to 13.99 mbpd, the highest since March. The TD3C premium, in turn, priced the difficulty of leaving the Gulf. Our numbers show who paid that premium: cargoes loaded inside the Strait, on TD3C, and buyers avoided those wherever they could. Crude prices set how much it bought: Brent rose from US$ 72.48 before the war to an intraday high of about US$ 126 on 30 April, and Chinese buying only recovered once it fell below US$ 80 in the summer. September showed the first sustained sign of demand pulling on that system, as freight for VLCCs loading in the Gulf of Oman (TD34) tripled m-o-m, faster than TD3C inside the Strait. The number of VLCCs ballasting towards West Africa, Brazil and the US Gulf fell from about 85 a week in early September to 50 to 54 since mid-October, while transfers off Oman ran at their limits.

items.title: Newbuildings head for Asia-Latin America trades as volumes boom
items.original_title: Newbuildings head for Asia-Latin America trades as volumes boom
items.summary: Deliveries in the past week have been primarily deployed to services between the Far East and Latin America, highlighting growing volumes on these trades. Alphaliner noted that Imabari Shipbuilding completed the 13,932 teu ONE Symphony that will be deployed on ONE’s Asia-WCSA AX3 service the pan-Japanese carrier runs jointly with MSC and Hapag-Lloyd. This is the 14th in a series of at least 15 vessels that various Imabari Group yards are building for ONE. MSC took delivery of the 10,300 teu MSC Licia X from Zhoushan Changhong International Shipyard, and will assign the ship to its solo Far East-East Coast of South America Carioca loop that deploys a fleet of 15 ships of between 8,000 and 12,000 teu capacity. MSC ordered the series in August 2023 for around $130m per unit. This is the second of four sisters commissioned in 2024 for $108m each, all for long-term charter to Zim. The Garnet will be assigned to the newly launched Far East-east coast South America ZFS service Zim runs with Hapag-Lloyd, part of a sustained shake-up of vessel sharing agreements on the Asia-South America trades , and features a port rotation of Shanghai-Ningbo-Xiamen-Hong Kong-Yantian-Rio Grande-Paranagua-Itajai-Santos-Rio de Janeiro. So far, ZFS is served by vessels in the size range from 5,500 to 9,000 teu, with both carriers acting as vessel providers.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: CargoWise customs message delays leave forwarders waiting for clearance
items.original_title: EXCLUSIVE: CargoWise customs message delays leave forwarders waiting for clearance
items.summary: CargoWise users handling British and Japanese customs declarations suffered messaging delays on Wednesday, while the backlog had been fully cleared the following morning. Customer notifications seen by The Loadstar show WiseTech acknowledged an issue affecting message responses at 10.37am on 28 October. At 11.24, it confirmed that GB and Japan customs messaging were “particularly impacted”. One UK forwarder said the disruption prevented its team from processing customs entries normally for much of the working day, leaving customers waiting and staff struggling to provide useful information. Subsequent updates at 12.04 and 14.07pm said engineers were working on mitigation, before a 3.51pm notice reported backlogs ‘processing slowly’. At 8.47pm, the company said the backlog across most queues had been processed, but teams remained ‘engaged on the core issue’ and working towards full restoration. At 8.33am yesterday, it confirmed that the backlog had been fully processed, and messaging services had recovered. The notifications span almost 22 hours, between acknowledgement and recovery confirmation, although they do not establish how long individual customers had been affected. The disruption follows a separate CargoWise outage reported by The Loadstar in June, when customers in several countries experienced log-in failures and electronic messaging problems.
